explanation.text: Your LinkedIn profile is a web page about you. When someone finds you, they usually read only the top part: your photo, your headline, and the first lines of your About section. So those few lines must work hard.
**The headline** is the line under your name. Do not write only "Student" or "Looking for opportunities". Say what you do and what you build or help with.
**The About section** can be short. A good order is:

items: Who you are and what you do now, in one or two plain sentences.
Proof: what you have built or learned. Name a real project.
What you want next, and how people can contact you.

explanation.text: Only the first lines show before the reader taps "see more". Put your best sentence first.
**The Featured section** lets you pin links. Pin your best project (a GitHub page or a write-up) and your best post.
**Skills**: list the skills you can show. If you are still learning something, say "learning". Honest and specific is stronger than a long list.
Show, do not claim. "Built a Python script that cleans a customer list" is stronger than "Python expert". A real thing you did is proof. A big word is only a claim.
Never copy someone else's profile text, and never write something that is not true. Employers check. A small true story beats a big false one.

explanation.title: About section
explanation.text: Fill in the brackets with your own true details, then delete any line that does not fit you.
explanation.code:
I am learning [your main skill] by building small [kind of tools] that [what they help with].

My latest project: [one sentence about a real project and what it does].

I am currently learning [next thing]. I am looking for [what you want next, in plain words].

You can contact me here on LinkedIn or at [email].

quiz.question: Which headline tells a reader the most?
options: Learning Python | Building small tools that clean business data
quiz.explanation: It says what you do and what you build. The others could describe anyone.

quiz.question: What should the first lines of your About section do?
options: Say clearly who you are and what you build
quiz.explanation: Most people read only the first lines, so make them count.

quiz.question: Why is "Built a script that cleans a customer list" stronger than "Python expert"?
options: It shows something real you did
quiz.explanation: A real result is proof. "Expert" is only a claim.
